messages:
mike: quick brain dump of a follow-up idea: lightweight tenant bypass tokens + hysteresis for prefetch suppression, tied into allocator demote hints. goal: reduce tiny, wasteful prefetch IOs during host stress without hurting critical requests.

anya: sounds promising. how do tokens work? do tenants get a burst budget?

mike: yes — each tenant gets N tokens per interval. prefetches marked critical always consume zero tokens; non-critical prefetches consume one token each. when tokens exhausted, non-critical prefetches are downgraded and subject to cooldown windows. tokens replenish slowly so a noisy tenant can't flood IO.

rod: where do we get the allocator demote hint? is that synchronous?

mike: allocator emits hint DEMOTE_PENDING when it schedules a slab demotion/evict. prefetch manager subscribes and treats any prefetch for pages in the demote set as conflict events that increment the tenant's stall counter.

anya: stall counter -> cooldown, right? what's the hysteresis to avoid flip-flop during short spikes?

mike: use exponential decay with a half-life and a per-tenant EWMA on host-io-queue-depth. only enter cooldown if both stall_count > threshold AND ewma_queue_depth > q_threshold. exit cooldown when stall_count decays below threshold/2 and ewma < q_threshold*0.8.

jin: fragmentation concern: if we coalesce aggressively when cooling down, we might pull page ranges that trigger compaction later. any guard?

mike: coalesce only merges prefetch IOs (read-only) and we cap adjacent-range expansion by host_fragmentation_ratio. if fragmentation_ratio > 0.55 we disable window expansion. write-path compaction remains unchanged.

rod: interaction with runtime batcher and GPU driver? want to avoid double-coalescing.

mike: the hint model: prefetch manager emits priority hint (high/low/defer). runtime batcher will accept low/defer and try to fold into next batch window; if driver-level coalescing exists, it will override and merge as before. low priority just tells software not to force immediate IO.

anya: metrics to observe in canary?

mike: pref.tokens.used{tenant}, pref.cooldown.count, pref.cooldown.duration_ms hist, host.io_qdepth, host.fragmentation_ratio, alloc.hints.demote_pending.count. alert if avg cooldown duration > 150ms or tokens.used spikes 3x baseline.

ops-bot: ci/6222 passed  includes token logic + unit tests.

jin: test plan: unit tests for token refill and decay, sim that replays mixed-tenant traces with slow-tier latencies, small cluster e2e with fio slow-tier. include attacker scenario where one tenant tries to burn tokens.

rod: rollout: feature-flagged, dedicated canary pool 5% for 6h, expand to 20% for 24h. rollback if p99 generation latency increases >6% or host fragment ratio increases >7%.

mike: will add per-pool opt-out and operator kill-switch. also doc blurb for hint semantics. opening PR and will tag you.

anya: nice—one nit: call the metric pref.token.refill_rate to be explicit.

mike: done, thanks.
